basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 12.' and it opens '(Cap. XXVI.—Vers. 12.) Seminavit autem Isaac in terra illa, et invenit in anno illo'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXVI.—Vers. 12.) Seminavit autem Isaac in terra illa, et invenit in anno illo centuplum hordei. Licet in aliena terra seminaverit Isaac, tamen non puto, quod tanta ei fertilitas hordei fuerit. Unde melius puto illud esse, quod habetur in Hebraeo, et Aquila quoque transtulit: Et invenit in anno illo centuplum aestimatum, id est, ἑκατὸν εἰκασμένον. Licet enim eisdem litteris et aestimatio scribatur et hordeum, tamen aestimationes, SAARIM (שערים) leguntur, hordea vero SORIM. Tacens autem Scriptura genus frugum, quod centuplicaverit, videtur mihi cunctarum in illo virtutum ostendisse multiplicationem. Denique sequitur:
